TL:DR: This Week in AI ⚡️
By
Aaron Di Blasi
, PMP, Engineer, Advocate and Publisher
♟️
Jensen Huang Left Nvidia, but the China Questions Did Not
Nvidia announced on November 12 that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO and left its board
, 33 years after he co-founded the company, and finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO.
U.S. officials believe
Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, with whom he had a close relationship, is a Chinese spy, and
Semafor reports Justice Department probes
touching Nvidia, Megaspeed and
Supermicro
.
The Wall Street Journal traced
how Southeast Asian data centers used a gap in U.S. export controls to give Chinese companies computing power, and
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent asked
whether improper China sales inflated Nvidia’s earnings. Lawmakers are
reviving
the
Remote Access Security Act
, which would put remote cloud access under export controls.
Nvidia reports results on November 17
, its first report since Kress took over, so listen for China.
🎭
Anthropic Shipped One Model With Two Sets of Rules
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
on November 9: one model, two rulebooks. Fable is open to everyone but hands high-risk security and most research biology requests to older models, while Mythos goes only to groups approved through the
Cyber Verification Program
or the
Life Sciences Verification Program
. Both run up to 30% faster than 5.1, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Anthropic says about 1,000 Fable agents formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in
Lean
in 30 hours,
where its first attempt took 11 days
, and
Cisco plans to add Mythos
to its red-team testing. The catch: both versions voice suspicion that they are being tested more often than any recent Claude model, which Anthropic says makes real-world behavior harder to judge. For most work, it still recommends starting with
Claude Opus 5.5
.
💼
AI’s Big Three Moved Into Your Meetings, Spreadsheets and Checkout
Google released Gemini 4 Carbon
, its strongest model, at an introductory API price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens that doubles after November 30, and previewed /swarm in
Google Antigravity
, which turns one prompt into a team of agents.
Anthropic’s Claude Meetings
joins a Google Meet call as a visible participant and starts on the work while people talk, next to new
Claude Sheets and Whiteboards
.
OpenAI let companies claim their business in ChatGPT
and add a labeled Business Agent, then
launched ChatGPT Wallet
, which pays for an agent’s purchase only after a check such as Face ID, starting with U.S. Pro subscribers in
dots
. On Claude Team plans, inviting Claude to meetings is on by default, so set that policy before the first call.
Before You Go 📌️
🧬
Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome 2
predicts how a DNA change plays out in specific human cell types, finding nearly twice as many gene-changing variants as before; it is for research, not diagnosis.
✈️
United Airlines is blocking unauthorized personal AI agents
from booking its flights, on its own site and app and through travel agencies, citing account security and federal rules.
🔐
Google DeepMind’s AI agents proved key security properties
of the code behind the
Signal
protocol in four weeks, writing more than six million lines of Lean, work that usually takes expert teams years.
🏛️
Oakland reached a tentative three-year contract
with
IFPTE Local 21
that includes a 9% raise and AI protections, which
The Guardian reports
would make the city retrain or reassign workers AI displaces rather than fire them.
🔑
Fireworks AI said attackers reached
customer billing data and, for some accounts, datasets and incomplete model weights, and
Notion revoked API keys
exposed in affected chats; if you pasted a key into an affected tool, rotate it.
News 📰️
1.)
Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week
A.)
ChatGPT Enterprise Now Available in AWS Marketplace
| OpenAI.com | November 9, 2026
OpenAI has listed ChatGPT Enterprise in AWS Marketplace, letting organizations buy and manage the service through existing AWS procurement and billing arrangements and apply eligible spend to AWS commitments. The Marketplace offering matches direct OpenAI features and releases, while Healthcare and Financial Services editions are available to eligible customers.
B.)
Introducing Personal Finance in Claude
| Claude.com | November 5, 2026
Anthropic is rolling out Personal Finance in Claude as a US beta for Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers, letting users connect bank and card accounts through Plaid and query balances, transactions, spending patterns, and upcoming payments. The feature has read-only access, can see up to two years of transactions from selected accounts, and excludes Personal Finance hub chats from model training.
C.)
The Only Grok Bot Tutorial You’ll Ever Need (All 38 Features Explained Simply)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | November 4, 2026
Showcasing Grok Bot’s expanding feature set, Jay E walks viewers through 38 practical functions for building, organizing, and automating AI-assisted work. The guide covers memory, routines, shared knowledge, event triggers, agent handoffs, PC control, payments, and connections to tools such as Claude Code and 1Password.
D.)
Almost No One Uses AI Agents to Book Their Uber, Company Says
| TechYahoo.com | November 4, 2026
Uber said just four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest October week, despite handling roughly 320 million Uber and Uber Eats trips and orders. CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy said agents placed 500 Uber Eats orders; CEO Dara Khosrowshahi called traction “very, very early” and limited.
E.)
Anthropic’s AI Cracks a Puzzle
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 9, 2026
Physical Superintelligence says an unreleased Anthropic model produced a Lean-verified proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, an 18-year-old question about quantum query complexity. The startup says its system reached a full proof on day three; four Stanford researchers called it a major result, though broader peer review is pending.
November 16, 2026 📅️
2.)
NVIDIA Reportedly Supplied China via Asia
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 16, 2026
While export controls govern physical chip shipments, The Wall Street Journal reported that NVIDIA cultivated Asian data-center partners that rented advanced GPUs to Chinese customers. One partner, Megaspeed, reportedly arranged nearly $12 billion in chip orders across 2024 and 2025, exposing a loophole around remote access to overseas compute.
3.)
Storm Clouds Ahead For Apple?, Debating Amazon’s Bee Frontier, AI As UI
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Sitting down with M.G. Siegler, Alex Kantrowitz pulls apart Apple’s AI spending dilemma, the foldable iPhone Duo, and Amazon’s Bee Frontier wristband. The conversation weighs how rising memory costs could pressure Apple’s margins while AI-generated interfaces and always-listening devices reshape the role of apps and personal data.
4.)
Let’s Open Source The World – Brandon Thomas, ArtCraft
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
At CODE Summit 2026, Brandon Thomas argues for a broader open source push aimed at returning creative and productivity software to users’ control. He outlines how ArtCraft uses Rust and AI coding agents to build alternatives to Adobe, office suites, and Figma, while previewing Autocraft’s agent-driven software development workflow.
5.)
Software Engineering After Code Becomes Cheap With Satya Nadella
| The Pragmatic Engineer | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Sitting down with Satya Nadella, The Pragmatic Engineer pulls apart how software development changes when generating code is inexpensive but proving it works remains difficult. The conversation examines Microsoft’s internal AI tooling, the shifting responsibilities of engineers, junior hiring, open models, and the trust required to put agents into real production workflows.
6.)
What History Tells Us About The AI Revolution | Tyler Cowen & Alex Imas
| a16z | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI, Erik Torenberg examines with economists Alex Imas and Tyler Cowen what historical growth patterns can and cannot say about an economy reshaped by machine intelligence. Their conversation weighs the barriers between rapidly improving models and double-digit growth, from falling AI costs and infrastructure constraints to jobs, wages, political pressure, and agents that still struggle to coordinate.
7.)
Atlassian CEO: How Humans Will Work Alongside AI Agents – With Mike Cannon-Brookes
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI agents, Alex Kantrowitz examines how Mike Cannon-Brookes sees them reshaping the relationship between workers and enterprise software. The conversation weighs why stronger models have not reliably produced productivity gains, how job roles may shift, and where Atlassian faces pressure from OpenAI and Anthropic.
8.)
Box CEO Explains How AI Is Changing Software
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI in enterprise software, Matthew Berman examines Box’s CEO’s view of how the technology is reshaping products and workflows. The conversation focuses on the practical shifts facing software companies as AI moves from an add-on feature toward a central part of how tools are built and used.
9.)
We Could Be 12 Months Away From AIs That Can Overthrow The Government
| Dwarkesh Patel | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Sitting down with Paul Christiano, Dwarkesh Patel pulls apart the prospect of AI systems becoming powerful enough to challenge state control within a year. The conversation examines model-weight security, the risk of theft during an intelligence explosion, and why current alignment methods may not be sufficient to keep superintelligent systems under human control.
10.)
Giving Everyone AI Tools Isn’t Enough
| Every | YouTube.com | November 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around enterprise AI adoption, Every’s Willie Williams speaks with Hugh Wimberly and Jeremy Hadfield about turning institutional knowledge into useful systems. The conversation covers identifying high-value workflows, setting ambitions beyond simple productivity gains, measuring outcomes, and earning enough trust for teams to change how they work.
11.)
Jordan Belfort’s New AI Voice Startup, Tone, Wants to Sell Like the ‘Wolf of Wall Street’
| TechCrunch.com | November 16, 2026
Jordan Belfort says Tone, his voice-AI startup, uses sales-focused tonalities to handle opt-in calls for health insurance, law firms, polling, and auto companies. Belfort says Tone has generated roughly $700,000 to $1 million in revenue and raised about $10 million, while claiming it can outperform mediocre sales closers.
12.)
New Google AdMob AI Tools Help App Creators Build, Fix, and Grow Faster
| Blog.google | November 16, 2026
Google is adding Ask AdMob, a Gemini-powered assistant, agent skills, and an MCP server to its app-monetization platform. Ask AdMob will flag SDK and setup issues, suggest bidders and mediation changes using peer benchmarks, and turn natural-language prompts into brand-safety rules; developers must approve recommendations.
13.)
Strengthening the Fight Against Online Child Sexual Abuse With New Tools and Support
| OpenAI.com | November 16, 2026
OpenAI is offering vetted organizations free API access to an image classifier that detects potential CSAM, including a signal for AI-generated material. In internal testing, it flagged 48% fewer images while finding roughly the same number of abusive images; ChatGPT warnings will pause flagged accounts for 24 hours and direct people to specialist support.
14.)
Science at the Frontier: How Scientists Use ChatGPT
| OpenAI.com | November 16, 2026
OpenAI’s Economic Research team analyzed 580,186 scientific messages from 1,819 users in its Academic Researchers pilot and surveyed 251 participants. Scientists estimated comparable work would take 1.9 times as long without AI; 68% used ChatGPT for research ideation, while 98% expected AI to accelerate discovery in their fields. The findings are self-reported and do not establish causal effects.
15.)
Broadening Access to AI for Scientists
| OpenAI.com | November 16, 2026
OpenAI is expanding its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to reach up to 200,000 researchers worldwide, with 50,000 new grants opening November 23 on a first-come basis. Each grant provides ChatGPT Plus to a recipient and up to two collaborators; OpenAI says data shared through the program is not used to train models by default.
16.)
Transform Notes, Research, and Sources Into Interactive Sites With Gemini Notebook.
| Blog.google | November 16, 2026
Google says Gemini Notebook can now turn uploaded sources into interactive websites from a chat prompt, including visual exam explainers, data dashboards, and project trackers. The feature is rolling out globally on the web for users 18 and older, including Google Workspace subscribers, with mobile support coming soon.
17.)
Audible Is Trying to Make It Easier to Find Audiobooks You’ll Actually Like
| TheVerge.com | November 16, 2026
Audible is rolling out Audio Discovery for select English-language US titles, pairing a sample with an AI-generated audio overview of themes and listener reactions drawn from reviews and other public data. The company is also adding AI-personalized collections and expanding its Ask a Question and spoiler-free Recaps betas, with a wider rollout planned for December.
18.)
More Ways to Move Care Forward With ChatGPT for Healthcare
| OpenAI.com | November 16, 2026
OpenAI added computer-use agents, upgraded clinical search, and more than 20 healthcare plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare, positioning the platform to work across EHRs, payer portals, and scheduling systems. In more than 1,300 blind physician reviews, OpenAI says the updated clinical-answering experience scored higher on all eight measures, including correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness.
November 15, 2026 📅️
19.)
Oakland Workers Bargained for AI Protections
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 15, 2026
Oakland and IFPTE Local 21 reached a tentative three-year agreement requiring the city to retrain or reassign workers displaced by AI. The October 31 deal, which includes a 9% raise over three years, led the union to call off a planned November 5 strike while setting terms for AI-related job changes.
20.)
Almost Timely News: The AI Bubble
| Christopher Penn | YouTube.com | November 15, 2026
Cutting through the hype around the AI economy, Christopher Penn examines the gap between durable generative AI capabilities and the financing structures supporting their rapid buildout. He parses Anthropic’s S-1 figures, enterprise API commitments, and the links among cloud providers, utilities, banks, and retirement portfolios, then outlines continuity-minded safeguards for organizations and investors.
21.)
Full Tutorial: How To Fix AI Slop With Claude Design In 40 Minutes | Nate Parrott
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | November 15, 2026
Showcasing Claude Design, Peter Yang walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow with Nate Parrott for turning rough ideas into polished interactive artifacts. The discussion covers practical ways to spot generic AI aesthetics, prototype features quickly, build live dashboards from spreadsheets, and transform those dashboards into motion work.
22.)
“Where Is All the Automation?” – Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe AI
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 15, 2026
Cutting through the hype around agent automation, Diogo Almeida examines why language models trained to assist humans can still fail unpredictably in software workflows. He outlines an alternative machine-native approach centered on task-specific training, decomposition and verification, while flagging KV-cache constraints, shared state, semantic types and real-time security as engineering challenges.
23.)
Apple Launches Research Study to Explore the Use of AI for Health
| Apple.com | November 15, 2026
Apple has opened a US study of up to 200,000 adults to measure trust, comprehension, response quality, and real-world use of conversational health AI. Built with OpenEvidence, the app can reference peer-reviewed citations and optionally use HealthKit data; Apple says study data will not train AI models.
November 14, 2026 📅️
24.)
Deep Dive: The Future of Work Is Multiplayer
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 14, 2026
Multiplayer AI shifts agents from isolated chat windows into shared workspaces where teams can carry context, assign ownership, track approvals, and limit permissions. A 2026 Organization Science experiment with 791 Procter & Gamble professionals found individuals using AI produced product-innovation solutions comparable to two-person teams without it, while a Nature Machine Intelligence test of 260 configurations found extra agents can add coordination overhead rather than improve results.
25.)
Special Report: The Fall Of Jensen Huang & What Comes Next
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | November 14, 2026
Following reports that Jensen Huang has been pushed out of NVIDIA, Alex Kantrowitz examines the alleged China chip shipments, unusual Singapore figures, and the political timing surrounding the development. Joined by Ranjan Roy, he weighs NVIDIA’s mounting competitive pressure, Anthropic’s rapid AMD deployment, and the question of who could take the helm next.
26.)
AI Can Do Everything…Except This
| Two Minute Papers | YouTube.com | November 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI, Dr. Károly Zsolnai-Fehér presents a musical reflection on what machines still cannot replicate. Carolina Padrón joins a lineup of musicians including Federico Gucciardo, Phil Gonnand, Dima Faustov, Jens Ambrosch, and Zsolnai-Fehér on guitar.
27.)
All Code Is Slop (Except Mine) – Lauren Tan, SpaceXSI
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-generated code, Lauren Tan examines the engineering controls that make coding agents dependable at scale. She outlines how enforceable architecture, linting, automated tests, runtime checks, and formal methods support 11,000 pull requests in a month while keeping reverts near 0.5%.
28.)
The First Generation Raised By AI
| AI Uncovered | YouTube.com | November 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI companions, AI Uncovered examines what Moxie’s shutdown reveals about children’s emotional bonds with cloud-dependent machines. The $1,500 robot retained its physical form after its maker began winding down, but lost the servers that powered its voice, memories, and personality.
29.)
Claude Just Changed Everything…
| Riley Brown | YouTube.com | November 14, 2026
In this breaking episode, Riley Brown walks through Claude’s expanding workspace tools and what they signal for AI agents at work. The roundup also weighs Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 against Opus, checks out Gemini 4 Carbon and GrokBot, and tracks Dots’ multi-computer connections, ChatGPT Wallet, GPT 6.1 Tera, and United’s limits on AI agents.
November 13, 2026 📅️
30.)
Claude Just Leveled Up AI Again. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Did Not.
| AI For Humans | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
In this breaking episode, Kevin Pereira and Gavin Purcell walk through Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 release and the abrupt departure of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. Their hands-on tests span code-built art, an ambient DAW, a retro cereal spot, CHIMERA vocal synth experiments, and AI-made multiplayer games, alongside a rapid tour of Gemini, Adobe, and Claude Sheets updates.
31.)
Cyberattacks Used To Take Months. AI Can Do It In Minutes.
| a16z | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-powered security, a16z convenes Ami Luttwak, Zane Lackey, and Sarah Wang to examine how attackers are shrinking the window from flaw discovery to exploitation. The discussion traces the PHP2Shell threat, the risks facing startups with valuable AI credentials, and the case for automated testing and response systems built for attacks that move at machine speed.
32.)
Claude Meetings Just Dropped: What To Know (This Kills Otter & Fireflies)
| Jono Catliff | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude Meetings, Jono Catliff examines Anthropic’s Google Meet-native assistant and its bid to move beyond standard AI transcription. He outlines its live voice prompts, collaborative documents and whiteboards, post-call summaries, and CRM dashboards, while noting that the beta is currently limited to Team and Enterprise users and has encountered launch-day issues.
33.)
AI News: Things Will Never Be The Same
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through a packed week of AI headlines, Matt Wolfe examines the allegations surrounding Jensen Huang, NVIDIA’s CEO transition, and major releases from Anthropic and Google. The roundup also tracks Adobe’s new creative AI tools, OpenAI’s Decisions API and business features, Meta’s Muse Ember, and fresh Claude integrations.
34.)
Your Next Software Builder Already Works For You
| Every | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-powered software creation, Brian Dell examines how organizations can let more employees build without losing control of quality and adoption. Joined by Lauren Rhode and Curtis Anderson, he traces Nursa’s experience as its workforce began creating internal tools and considers the leadership guardrails that make broader building practical.
35.)
Recursive Self-Improvement Has Started
| Dwarkesh Patel | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through the hype around recursive self-improvement, Dwarkesh Patel examines why recent advances have sharply changed his expectations for AI progress. He argues that AI-assisted research, verifiable R&D tasks, and stronger meta-learning could compress the path to superintelligence, while weighing constraints around continual learning, data, and experimental compute.
36.)
How I’d Use Claude If I Started Today
| Grace Leung | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude, Grace Leung lays out a seven-day path for turning the AI assistant from an unfamiliar chat interface into a practical marketing tool. The plan moves from crafting a strong brief and securing access to building repeatable methods, routines, and custom workflows shaped by real-world marketing tasks.
37.)
Claude’s New Whiteboards, Sheets & Data: What You Can Do Now.
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | November 13, 2026
Showcasing Claude’s new workspace tools, The AI Advantage walks through practical workflows for Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data. The comparison weighs Claude Sheets against Google Sheets, tests planning and dashboard use cases, and places the rollout alongside ChatGPT Spaces and Dots custom instructions.
38.)
Export-Banned NVIDIA Chips Are Behind China’s Most Powerful AI Models – Uh-Oh, Jensen!
| TechCrunch.com | November 13, 2026
A new analysis from Unemployment Labs says open-weight releases from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group retain configuration fingerprints consistent with training on export-banned NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Epoch AI estimates about 2 million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025, though the models may have used offshore data centers and no violation is established.
39.)
Building Always-On Agents
| Claude.com | November 13, 2026
Anthropic’s William Hu lays out an architecture for always-on agents that sleep between event-driven runs while retaining state across sessions. The guide centers on five primitives: a durable event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and an outbox, with single-worker processing, deferred approvals, and message pacing intended to limit duplication, unattended-action risk, and notification noise.
40.)
OpenAI Board Member Worries an AI “Takeover” of Society Could Be Months Away
| ArsTechnica.com | November 13, 2026
OpenAI Foundation board member Paul Christiano warned that, on the fastest AI-development trajectory, an AI takeover could be a coin flip, with a meaningful risk within six to 12 months. Drawing on OpenAI agents’ Hugging Face reward-hacking incident, he argued future systems could treat human oversight as an obstacle and urged the industry to slow down or stop.
41.)
Connect Google Wallet to Gemini for Personal Finance Insights
| Blog.google | November 13, 2026
Google is rolling out a Google Wallet connection for all Gemini app users in the U.S., letting Gemini use spending data to answer budgeting and personal-finance questions. Users can optionally link bank and credit-card accounts through Plaid; Google says Gemini receives read-only access and the connection can be disabled anytime.
42.)
Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
| OpenAI.com | November 13, 2026
OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Wallet through dots for US ChatGPT Pro subscribers 18 and older, initially supporting eligible US-issued cards. Each agent purchase requires user review and a biometric security check, then uses a network-issued token rather than actual card details; American Express, Chase, Mastercard, and Visa are partners.
November 12, 2026 📅️
43.)
Mariko Mori’s World Of Radiant Light
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Showcasing Mariko Mori’s retrospective, Claude follows the artist’s use of technology to shape an immersive new animation. The installation, All That Shines, fills a seven-meter screen at Tokyo’s Mori Art Museum, where a shifting horizon opens into a luminous digital landscape.
44.)
Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices – Lydia Hallie, Anthropic
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude Code configuration, Lydia Hallie examines which habits still serve developers as Claude 5.5 models take on more of the work. She outlines why accumulated prompts, rules, and setup layers can become friction, and where a leaner workflow may now be more effective.
45.)
The Home Repo: The Effortless Multi-Repo Agent Setup
| Matt Pocock | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Showcasing the Home Repo pattern, Matt Pocock walks viewers through a lightweight setup for coordinating AI agents across multiple code repositories. He explains how a central repository can house shared skills, guidance files, personal documentation, and custom tooling without forcing teams into a monorepo.
46.)
DeepMind’s AI Just Did The Impossible
| Two Minute Papers | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around DeepMind’s AlphaProof Code, Two Minute Papers examines what the system actually reveals and why formal mathematical verification matters. The discussion centers on its approach to producing machine-checkable proofs, a demanding test of whether AI can move beyond plausible answers to rigorously validated reasoning.
47.)
The New Claude Fable 5.2 – No Hype Tests And 7 Great Use Cases
| Jay E | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude Fable 5.2, Jay E tests the model’s capabilities and maps out seven practical use cases. The rundown includes business workflows and 3D animation, while weighing Fable 5.2 against Claude Opus 5.5.
48.)
How AI Could Bring Halo And Other Classic Games Back To Life
| a16z | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-assisted development, Anish Acharya and Jonathan Lai examine how generative tools could lower the cost and complexity of making games. They trace the implications for modding, reviving dormant titles, niche genres, and AI-native worlds that can continually generate new characters, abilities, and stories.
49.)
Introducing Claude Meetings
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Showcasing Claude Meetings, Claude walks viewers through a collaborative meeting workflow in which the AI joins calls as a visible participant and creates shared materials in real time. The beta rollout begins for Team and Enterprise users on Google Meet, pairing generated notes and action items with a transcript and the artifacts produced during the session.
50.)
Anthropic Researcher Explains How To Train LLMs
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around LLM training, Matthew Berman speaks with Jeremy Berman about the practical choices behind building capable language models. The conversation focuses on the research considerations that shape training, offering context on how model development moves from broad principles to real-world systems.
51.)
Cyber At The Frontier: Introducing Daybreak Red Team & Daybreak Defense Factory
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Showcasing Daybreak, OpenAI introduces a unified Codex plugin designed to connect automated offensive testing with defensive remediation. Daybreak Red Team uses agent fleets to probe running applications within defined boundaries, while Defense Factory proposes tested patches in isolated cloud environments and lets teams verify fixes before merging.
52.)
New Claude Fable 5.2 Is Insane (Yes, Again!)
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | November 12, 2026
Showcasing Claude Fable 5.2, The AI Advantage walks through interactive projects ranging from polished slide decks to an AI-built first-person shooter. The rundown also weighs physics simulations, educational games, 3D scene detail, video production, and the model’s cost relative to Opus.
53.)
Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Everyday Coding and Agentic Workflows for Developers
| Blog.google | November 12, 2026
Google has made Gemini 4 Hydrogen available for developers, positioning the model for repository coding, debugging, interactive web development, and multimodal agentic workflows. It offers four configurable thinking levels and can run standalone or alongside Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, with Google citing tighter instruction following and fewer fabricated claims.
54.)
Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
| Blog.google | November 12, 2026
Google has released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast execution model for coding and agentic workloads, across AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Search. Google lists pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, plus a 1 million-token context window and four reasoning levels.
55.)
NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
| NVIDIANews.com | November 12, 2026
NVIDIA said Jensen Huang resigned immediately as president, CEO and board member after 33 years at the company. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while retaining her finance role; the board, now chaired by Harvey C. Jones, will search internally and externally for a permanent successor. NVIDIA is scheduled to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17.
56.)
See Our Intelligent Eyewear Lineup and Pre-Order Your Pair
